record.field: Nunavut rates V by annual taxable income A, as [[threshold, rate], ...] (T4127 option 1, step 4, T4 = V x A - KP - K1P - K2P - K3P). 2026: 4% from 0, 7% from 55,801, 9% from 111,602, 11.5% from 181,439. The constant KP is derived from the table and rounded to the dollar like the federal K: 0, 1,674, 3,906, 8,442. The rate of the first bracket is the lowest territorial rate of K1P and K2P (0.04). Nunavut did not change on July 1, 2026. T4127 122nd edition (January 2026), table 8.1; 123rd edition (July 2026), table 8.1. Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/payroll/t4127-payroll-deductions-formulas/t4127-jan/t4127-jan-payroll-deductions-formulas-computer-programs.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/payroll/t4127-payroll-deductions-formulas/t4127-jul/t4127-jul-payroll-deductions-formulas.html

TCP of an employee who files no TD1NU: K1P = lowest territorial rate x TCP (0.04 x 19,659 = 786.36 in 2026). Nunavut has no income-tested basic personal amount. 2026: 19,659, indexation rate 2.0%. T4127 122nd edition (January 2026), table 8.2; TD1NU 2026 line 1. Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/payroll/t4127-payroll-deductions-formulas/t4127-jan/t4127-jan-payroll-deductions-formulas-computer-programs.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/payroll/t4127-payroll-deductions-formulas/t4127-jul/t4127-jul-payroll-deductions-formulas.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/td1-personal-tax-credits-returns/td1-forms-pay-received-on-january-1-later/td1nu.html

Payroll tax of the employee, withheld by the employer on each pay: tax = rate x the gross of the pay, rounded to the cent (salary rule CA_NU_PAYROLL_TAX). Payroll Tax Act (Nunavut), s. 3(1): "Every employee is liable to pay to the Government a tax in the amount equal to 2% of the remuneration paid to the employee in the year", 2% since January 1, 2007; s. 5(1): the employer collects it by deducting or withholding it from the remuneration. Government of Nunavut: "a withholding or 'pay-as-you-earn' payroll tax valued at 2% of all gross remuneration" (registration form, 2022); "Employers are required to withhold 2% of gross remuneration paid from each employee" (guide, 2011). Remuneration: the amounts included in employment income under s. 5(1), 6 and 7 of the Income Tax Act (Canada); not subject: members of religious orders with a vow of poverty, and an employee who normally works outside Nunavut and earns 5,000 or less a year in Nunavut (Payroll Tax Regulations, R-049-93, s. 2). 2026: 0.02. The current consolidation of the Act could not be read automatically. Sources: https://www.gov.nu.ca/sites/default/files/documents/2022-11/payroll_application_-_registration_feb_2022.pdf ; https://www.gov.nu.ca/sites/default/files/documents/2021-10/payroll_guide_-_guide_to_payroll_tax_withholding_and_reporting_-_web_december_2011.pdf ; https://www.nunavutlegislation.ca/en/media/99 ; https://www.gov.nu.ca/finance/information/payroll-taxes

Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration (YMIR) per worker in Nunavut: the assessable payroll of the pay is min(gross, maximum - assessable payroll of the year so far); assessment = (assessable payroll / 100) x the rate of the industry subclass. 2026: 117,300 (WSCC: "The 2026 Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration (YMIR) for the NWT is $116,000 and for Nunavut is $117,300"). Nunavut and the Northwest Territories have distinct maximums since 2025. The Nunavut regulation that sets the figure could not be read automatically. 2027 not published. Sources: https://wscc.nt.ca/employer-services/employer-rates ; https://wscc.nt.ca/employer-services/report-payroll ; https://www.nunavutlegislation.ca/en/consolidated-law/workers-compensation-general-regulations-consolidation
